title: Video desk, Wed Nov 25 set: Sector Scoreboard, Trading Explained (gross margin), AI This Week

general-counsel-agent.note: All ten checks on file after reviewing the three review sheets (sector scoreboard, gross-margin explainer, AI This Week), report.json spoken text, titles, captions and sources. Defamation screen: sectors and companies appear only with Webull data; no reason is given for any move, and the sector video says so. The two people named (Jakub Pachocki and Antonio Guterres; no private person) appear only with what two or more outlets report they said or proposed, in neutral words. Nothing commits the owner; delivery is to the owner only. AI review, not legal advice.

advertising-consumer-protection-counsel.note: Every number traces to a saved raw response or a cited source (factcheck.py: 0 unmatched; every bar and compare value re-checked against raw with its sign). Sectors: raw/00_get_market_sectors_D1.json and raw/01_get_market_sectors_D5.json, the 20 sectors returned in market-value order (16 of 20 up on the day, 13 of 20 down over 5 days). Gross margin: raw/02-08 get_income_statement (gross_profit / revenue; operating margin = op_income / revenue); Apple quarter ended Sep 26, 2026: 114,477M revenue - 59,657M cost = 54,820M gross profit = 47.89%. Definition: AccountingTools, Wall Street Prep, Patriot Software (with Wikipedia and Xero consistent). AI news: each story in 2+ independent outlets dated Nov 22-24, 2026 (within 14 days): Pachocki proposal (Quartz, Techstrong.ai, Digital Today, Epoch Times), Bridgetown summit (UN News, Rappler, Caribbean Today, Tech Times), Nuro/Lucid/Uber driverless tests (Quartz, The Next Web, Investing.com, GadgetReview, Nuro's own page). Claims are worded no stronger than the sources: 'a proposal, not a binding rule', 'no number yet', 'still testing', launch 'targeted for 2027'.

email-anti-spam-compliance-counsel.note: No commercial email. The delivery email goes to the owner only.

privacy-data-protection-counsel.note: No personal data. The only people named are public figures in their public roles; no private person is named or shown; the owner isn't named or shown.

copyright-fair-use-counsel.note: Visuals are drawn from data and text by the kit's renderer; the voice is Kokoro-82M (Apache-2.0); music is synthesized per video by music.py; fonts are Inter, Space Grotesk and JetBrains Mono (SIL OFL). News is summarized in our own words with credit; the one quote is seven words from a public statement (Guterres: 'not a treaty, it's not regulation'), attributed. No screenshots, logos, photos or third-party footage.

trademark-brand-clearance-counsel.note: Webull, Meta, Nvidia, Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Tesla, OpenAI, Nuro, Lucid (Gravity), Uber, the UN and the named outlets are used only to refer to them (nominative use); no logos; nothing suggests endorsement or affiliation. 'Mag 7' is a descriptive market nickname. Hashtags are generic topic tags (#OpenAI names the subject of the story).

financial-content-compliance-counsel.note: 'Educational only. Not financial advice.' is on screen at the end of the sector and gross-margin videos and in both captions. No buy/sell call, target, prediction or performance promise. The sector video shows what moved and says no reason is given; the explainer defines a ratio with real reported figures and makes no judgement on any stock. The AI news video makes no market or stock claims, so it carries no disclaimer.

platform-terms-policy-counsel.note: The narrator is a synthetic (AI) voice over data graphics: on Instagram and Facebook turn on the 'AI info' label. Nothing realistic depicts a real person, so YouTube's altered-content disclosure isn't triggered, but disclosing the AI voice is still the safer choice. No branded-content relationship exists. Titles match the content (no misleading metadata).

kids-content-coppa-counsel.note: All three are adult finance and tech-news content: not made for kids, no child appears, no child data is collected.

contracts-commercial-terms-counsel.note: No proposal, quote, offer or contract; nothing is sold or promised in these videos.

The explainer's Mag 7 bars first showed Apple and Tesla in amber (below 50%), which could read as a judgement with no legend; all seven bars are now the same green.

The lines were rewritten with the same numbers ('79 dollars and 31 cents', 'one hundred fourteen point four eight billion', percentages said with 'percent') and all three were re-rendered.
